articleTitle: Submillimeter, Millimeter and Microwave Spectral Line Catalogue
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A computer accessible catalogue of submillimeter, millimeter, and microwave spectral lines in the frequency range between 0 and 3000 GHz has been developed. The information listed for each spectral line includes the frequency and its estimated error, the intensity, lower state energy, and quantum number assignment. The catalogue has been constructed by using theoretical least squares fits of published spectral lines to accepted molecular models. The catalogue currently contains over 90,000 lines of 133 atomic and molecular species.

articleTitle: An Ultra Low-Noise Schottky Mixer Receiver at 80–120 GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An ultra low-noise mixer receiver has been developed at the Five College Radio Astronomy Observatory for astronomical observations from 80 to 120 GHz with the 13.7 m diameter millimeter telescope. The cryogenic front end consists of a feed horn, a ring filter and a waveguide mixer followed by a 1.4 GHz FET amplifier. The optimization of the mixer RF-impedance at 100 GHz has yielded single sideband (SSB) receiver noise temperatures of 1 24 K and 588 K at physical temperatures of 18 K and 295 K, respectively.

articleTitle: A Gyrotron Study Program
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Investigations on very high frequency high power generators at THOMSON-CSF cover different theoretical studies on gyrotron oscillator and amplifiers, the development of a 35 GHz single cavity gyrotron oscillator and theoretical studies on submillimetric generators.

articleTitle: On the Theory of Printed Circuit Antennas for Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This paper presents a basic theory for modeling printed circuit antennas for millimeter wave applications. Printed circuit dipoles are considered and the Pocklington integral equation is solved for the antenna current distribution. Substrates of arbitrary thickness and dielectric constant can be taken into account in this model and the precise contribution of surface wave modes to antenna parameters is discussed.

articleTitle: Planar Antenna-Coupled SIS Devices for Detection and Mixing
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In order to avoid the difficulties associated with waveguide and cat-whisker contacts at frequencies above 100GHz, a planar integrated circuit combining lead-alloy SIS junctions and a receiving antenna has been developed. A novel tuning device for the planar circuit will also be described.

articleTitle: Harmonic Generation in the Near-Millimeter-Wave Range by Thin MOS-Structures
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Concepts for frequency multiplication into the range of 200 - 600 GHz are described. They are based on MOS-diodes with extremely thin oxide- and Si-epi-layers. While the goal is planar integrated arrays, the first experiments are done with individual whisker-coupled diodes.

articleTitle: Submm Heterodyne Observations of the Sun, Moon, Jupiter and Orion at 691 GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A submm heterodyne receiver has been used for radiometric measurements of the sun, moon and Jupiter and for the detection of the CO J = 6 -> 5 rotational transition at 691 GHz. The observations were made with the 0.76 m Jungfraujoch telescope at 3,600 m on February 1981. In this paper we present high resolution observations and mapping of the sun between 393.6 μm and 513.0 μm and observations of the moon and Jupiter at 432.6 μm. The previously observed CO J = 6 -> 5 transition by Fetterman et al. (1) has been confirmed.

articleTitle: Application of Untuned Cavities for Millimeter Wave Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A theory of untuned cavities is presented which provides the possibility of measuring the complex index of refraction of strongly absorbing samples (K ≥ 0.1) and the absorption coefficient of weakly absorbing samples. We describe a newly developed spectrometer of this type for the broadband frequency regime from 40 GHz to 170 GHz and at temperatures ranging from 4.2°K to 300°K. This method seems to offer the only possibility for performing dielectric measurements on strongly scattering samples at mm- and sub-mm-waves. It has proved to be particularly useful for studies on biological objects such as macromolecules and cells.

articleTitle: A Cryogenic Receiver for 1 Mm Wavelength
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A cryogenic receiver covering the 200-350 GHz range is described. Two Schottkydiode mixers cover this range, with the mixers and FET IF amplifier cooled to 20 K. LO power is provided by a frequency doubler/tripler, with a Martin-Puplett interferometer used as the LO-signal diplexer. The best system temperature is 710 K SSB at 225 GHz, rising to 2000 K at 348 GHz.

articleTitle: 225 GHz Radar System
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A 225 GHz Radar Transceiver developed at Georgia Tech will be described and preliminary test results will be presented. The system was designed for coherent operation and features an extended interaction oscillator transmitter, a subharmonically pumped (f/4) receiver, and a quasi-optical duplexer.

articleTitle: Vivaldi Antenna/Fin-Line Circuit for SIS Mixers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We propose the use of a Vivaldi (exponentially tapered slot) antenna and a fin-line (or slot-line) circuit on the same substrate for coupling to SIS mixers at frequencies up to several hundred GHz. Measured data for scaled Vivaldi antennas are presented. We also show that the loss in superconducting fin-line circuits should be quite low over the frequency range considered.

articleTitle: Second-Harmonic One-Millimeter Gyromonotron
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Radiation at 238 GHz with peak power of the order of 50 W has been obtained from a second-harmonic gyromonotron. Initial measurements with a Fabry-Perot interferometer indicate a spectral width of at most a few MHz.

articleTitle: A Portable, All-Solid-State Low Noise Receiver for 230 GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A low-noise receiver for 300K ambient operation at 230 GHz is described. The receiver incorporates a single-ended, fixed tuned Schottky barrier diode mixer, a frequency tripled Gunn source as local oscillator and a GaAs FET I.F. amplifier. The single sideband receiver noise temperature is typically 1300K when the L.O. is tuned to any frequency between 210 and 240 GHz.

articleTitle: Crystal Quartz Etalons for FIR Laser Interferometer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Crystal quartz etalons are designed for the beam splitter and the window of a 118.8-μm CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH laser interferometer. Measured transmissivities of these etalons agree with estimated values within ± 2%. The measured refractive index and absorption coefficient derived from the transmissivity measurements for the extraordinary ray at 118.834 μm are 2.1695 ± 0.0004 and 0.50 ± 0.09 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency Tuning and Efficiency Enhancement of High Power FIR Lasers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: National Magnet Laboratory Massachusetts Institute of Technology Cambridge, Mass. 02139 Introduction Laser pumped molecular lasers have many useful applications including radar, plasma diagnostics and spectroscopy. This range of applications would be expanded considerably with the development of highly efficient and/or frequency tunable laser pumped lasers. In this paper, we describe techniques for achieving these goals, techniques based on excitation of a molecular gas far off resonance. We have already demonstrated such excitation in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser pumping of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F gas. Experimental and theoretical work has been carried out on a tunable far infrared (FIR) laser based on Raman scattering of tunable CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser pump radiation in molecular gases. Good agreement between theory and experiment is obtained. Stimulated multiphoton emission processes are considered as a method of achieving efficiency enhancement in laser pumped lasers. These processes achieve high efficiency through the simultaneous emission of several low frequency photons for each high frequency photon absorbed.

articleTitle: Conversion Efficiency and Noise Measurements of SIS Array Mixers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Quasiparticle heterodyne mixers which use series arrays [1] of Pb-alloy SIS tunnel junctions have been tested at 36 GHz. These arrays each showed a conversion loss of approximately 5dB. Single-sideband noise temperatures of 9.8 ± 5K, 34 ± 12 K, and 85 ± 25 K were measured for 1, 10 and 50 junction arrays respectively. Significantly increased saturation levels were observed for the 10 and 50 junction arrays.

articleTitle: Imaging Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A far-infrared imaging antenna array has been demonstrated for the first time. The array is a line of evaporated silver bow-tie antennas on a fused-quartz substrate with bismuth-micro-bolometer detectors. The measured optical transfer function shows that the system is diffraction-limited. This imaging array should find direct application in fusion plasma diagnostics. If the microbolometers can be replaced by more sensitive diode detectors, the array should also find application in radiometry and radar.

articleTitle: Investigation of Narrow Band-Gap Semiconductors for Tunnetts
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The potential of abrupt junction TUNNETT diodes made from narrow band gap semiconductor for millimeter wave frequency are explored theoretically. The alloy compound Hg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Cd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Te which has a tunable band gap is chosen in this study. Neglecting impact ionization, an efficiency of 2.5% is obtained at 94 GHz in the simulation with a band-gap of 0.41 eV. We suggest that narrow band gap semiconductors have good potential for fabricating diodes operating in the TUNNETT or MITATT modes for millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Cyclotron Maser Instability as a Resonant Limit of a Space Charge Wave
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In place of a treatment in phase space, we present in this paper a macroscopic, fluid-like, description of cyclotron maser instabilities in a simple geometrical configuration. The approach follows that commonly used in conventional microwave devices. The usual dispersion relationship for cyclotron maser instability is recovered by considering the synchronous interaction between the space charges on the relativistic beam with the surrounding electromagnetic structure. The charge bunching processes are described. This analysis is also valid for nonsynchronous interactions.

articleTitle: Nonradiative Dielectric Waveguide Circuit Components
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Basic circuit components based on the NRO-guide were fabricated and tested at 50 GHz. Measurements show that the NRD-guide is quite practical since the circuit components operate as expected withouts uffering from radiation and interference.

articleTitle: The Sulfur Dioxide SMMW Lasers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Submillimeter-wave (SMMW) laser action with gaseous sulfur dioxide has previously been obtained on three transitions of the optically pumped cw laser [1], and on ten transitions of the electric discharge laser [2]. We report 15 additional transitions of the optically pumped laser.

articleTitle: GaAs Abrupt Junction Mitatt and Tunnett
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We report a theoretical investigation on the GaAs abrupt pn junction diodes to be operated in the MITATT or TUNNETT mode from 100 GHz to 800 GHz. No maximum frequency limitation is found due to the effect of injection pulse width. The experimental results by Nishizawa et.al., are in agreement with the theory. Our results indicate that GaAs MITTATs or TUNNETTs can operate with significant efficiency, around 5%, at least up to 500 GHz.

articleTitle: Advances in Submillimeter-Wave Carcinotrons
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This paper is devoted to recent advances made at THOMSON-CSF in the field of millimeter-wave and submillimeter-wave carcinotrons (BWO's). They concern reduction in size and weight, and improvement in the life and reliability of carcinotrons, as well as the coverage of higher frequency bands, the latest model operating over a 400–500 GHz band. Technological problems and development objectives (tubes operating at up to 1000 GHz) will be discussed.

articleTitle: D2O Laser Thomson Scattering and Submillimeter Heterodyne Receiver Measurements
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The MIT program to develop high power collective Thomson scattering diagnostics will be presented. All elements of a 385 μm D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O laser Thomson scattering diagnostic are in place and operational on the Alcator C tokamak. Major components include: a 0.5 MW, 150 ns D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O laser; a heterodyne receiver using a corner reflector mounted Schottky diode mixer and a 25 mW, 381 μm DCOOD laser local oscillator; and x-band I.F. electronics including a 32 channel multiplexer filter centered at 9.4 GHz with 80 MHz wide channels. Receiver noise temperatures (not including signal collection optics) of 15,000-20,000 K double sideband (DSB) have been measured for individual filter channels. Additional details of the D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O laser, the receiver and the overall implementation of this diagnostic on Alcator C have been described previously [1-3].

articleTitle: Materials Implications on Millimeter Wave Radome Performance
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An evaluation of candidate millimeter wave (MMW) radome materials necessitated determination of measurement repeatability of the Fabry-Perot interferometer. Measurements took into account material orientation with respect to the applied field to study fiber orientation effects. Subsequently, theoretical calculations were performed to find the impact of these dielectric variations on missile radome performance.

articleTitle: Linear Theory of Gyromonotron
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: There have been a great number of papers concerning the linear theory of electron cyclotron resonance maser 1–6. The previous studies, however, have been limited or idealized in one respect or another. In this paper the general linear theory of gyromonotron is given with it's concrete application.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Amplification in the Negative Glow
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Gain measurements, resonator experiments, and theoretical modeling of the amplification of millimeter-wave radiation in the cathode-region plasma of a cold-cathode discharge are reported.

articleTitle: Collective Effects on the Operation of free Electron Lasers with an Axial Guide Field
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The linearized gain for a free electron laser is analyzed for a configuration in which an axial magnetic guide field is present in addition to the static helical wiggler field. It is assumed that the wiggler period is much greater than the electron beam radius and, hence, we neglect radial variations in the wiggler field amplitude. The treatment of the gain proceeds from a solution of the Vlasov-Maxwell equations, and is divided into two parts. The first part deals with the gain for a tenuous beam in the small-signal regime. Collective effects arising from relatively dense beams are discussed in the last part.

articleTitle: The Far Infrared Reflectance of Optical Black Coatings
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Far infrared specular reflectance spectra of six optically black coatings near normal incidence are presented. The spectra were obtained using 9 bandpass transmission filters in the wavelength range between 12 and 300 microns. Data on the construction, thickness, and rms surface roughness of the coatings are also presented. The chemical composition of two coatings can be distinguished from that of the others by a strong absorption feature between 20 and 40 microns which is attributed to amorphous silicate material. Inverse relationships between these spectra and coating roughness and thickness are noted and lead to development of a single reflecting-layer model for the measured reflectance. The model is applied to the spectra of several coatings whose construction falls within its constraints.

articleTitle: New Ideas for Efficient Generation of Coherent Near-Millimeter Wave Radiation
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Production of efficient sources of coherent near millimeter wave (NMMW) radiation is an important unsolved prohlem. In the most efficient devices at present, optically pumped lasers and gas-discharge systems such as the HCN laser, excitation supplied at energy \hslash \omega ∼ leV produces NMMW photons of energy \hslash \omega ∼ 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> ev, the remainder of the excitation energy being trapped in the molecule. This leads to an intrinsic reduction ξ o = \Omega/ \omega ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> in power conversion efficiency, since in these systems, each excitation quantum yields at best one NMMW photon.

articleTitle: A Method for Optimizing the RF Field Distribution in a Gyromonotron
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The maximum efficiency of a gyromonotron depends on the RF field and the static magnetic field distributions in the resonator. A method for optimizing the RF field distribution is presented. The possibility of realizing this optimized field distribution by employing a magnetic field step will be studied.

articleTitle: Correction of Phase Errors in far Infrared Fourier Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In an ideal two-beam interferometer, the interferogram is the cosine Fourier transform of the frequency spectrum of the light detected by the detector. The ideal case represented by equations we start out with here seldom occurs in practice. Phase errors are introduced into the measurement of the interferogram by systematic errors in the path difference (i.e. missing the origin when the interferogram is sampled; this error is probably the most common one), by misalignment of the interferometer, and by intrinsic asymmetry between the interferometer arms. The measured interferogram is the product y(x)A(x,L1,L2) where A(x,Ll,L2) is a truncation and apodization function. This function has an inverse Fourier transform. Our procedure for choosing A(x,Ll,L2) and for phase correction is presented.

articleTitle: A Segmented Aperture Approach to High Resolution NMMW Imaging
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A design concept for a high resolution near millimeter wave imaging system is described. The design yields the required resolution for ground fire control applications with a series of small circular apertures which emulate a single large aperture. Design performance is analyzed and simulated imagery as shown.

articleTitle: Magnetic Resonances in Perovskite-Type Layer Structures
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In addition to our recent investigations of Rb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, we have studied the antiferromagnetic resonance of similar manganese compounds with longer hydrocarbon chains, namely (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with n = 2,3 and NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>MnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> with m = 2,4,5. Our essential result from these magnetic resonance measurements in the millimeter wave range is that the zero field antiferromagnetic resonance frequency decreases drastically for increasing chain lengths, i.e. for increasing separation of the magnetic layers in these compounds.

articleTitle: Near-Millimeter Wave Studies of Sub-Micron Layers of Doped Gallium Arsenide
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The near-millimeter wave optical properties of doped GaAs films on high resistivity GaAs substrates have been studied. These measurements are compared to a Drude free carrier model and the electrically measured properties.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Radiometer System for an Atmospheric Research Satellite
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Design of the radiometers being developed for the Microwave Limb Sounder instrument tentatively selected for the Upper Atmospheric Research Satellite will be described. Total power radiometers are planned to operate in five spectral bands centered at 63, 119, 183, 205 and 233 GHz to measure several atmospheric parameters.

articleTitle: Intracavity Pumped FIR NH3 Laser by te CO2 Laser
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A compact FIR laser cavity having a couple of folding mirrors was designed. By inserting this FIR cavity into the pump TE CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser resonator, we observed 19 FIR NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> laser lines. The maximum output power was over 100 W at 150 μm and 90 μm lines.

articleTitle: Magnetic Excitations in Rb2CrxMn1-xCl4 Mixed Crystals
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Solid solutions of Rb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CrCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and Rb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> are of particular interest since there are not only competing anisotropy energies due to the single ion anisotropy of Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> but also competing exchange interactions. We have studied the magnetic excitations of Rb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> mixed crystals by means of magnetic resonance in the concentration range 0.02 < x < 0.41 where there is a long range antiferromagnetic order different from that of pure Rb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and in the concentration range 0.41 < x < 0.59 where there is no long range order. Our results in the latter range confirm a spin glass behavior at low temperatures. In the antiferromagnetic range, our results provide information about the exchange interactions and the anisotropy fields.

articleTitle: Anomalous Stress Shift of Impurity Lines in Te under High Pressure
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: For the elementary semiconductor Tellurium the effects of hydrostatic and uniaxial stress are in many aspects complementary. Whereas for hydrostatic pressure the helical chains of the lattice cell are pressed together and slightly expanded along the symmetry axis, for uniaxial stress along this axis holds exactly the opposite. This behaviour is well reflected by the complementary distortion of the electronic energy band states and has been confirmed experimentally by cyclotron resonance experiments [1]. The present study investigates whether the same complementary situation holds also for the shallow impurity system and provides eventually a tool for the still remaining identification of the different impurity transitions.

articleTitle: Some Recent Developments in CW Optically Pumped FIR Lasers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: As pointed out in 1978 by Hodges at the Third International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves [1], a review of advances in optically pumped FIR lasers (OPFIRL's) since the pioneering work of Chang and Bridges[2] represents a formidable challenge; how much more so today when six full sessions were devoted to the subject at the Fifth International Conference in Wrzburg [3]. Since good review articles already exist [1,4,5,6], it is not the purpose of the present paper to be encyclopaedic, but rather to outline some developments in the last two years. Detailed references will be given in the text; a comprehensive source is in work already cited [3,6] or in the Journal of IR and Mm Waves [7]. Again for reasons of space, it is necessary to adhere strictly to advances in cw OPFIRL's.

articleTitle: High Contrast Multipass Fabry-Perot Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Although diffraction grating and Fourier Transform spectrometers are widely used in the infrared & far infrared, both techniques posses inherent disadvantages. It is well-known that the radiation throughput of the grating spectrometer is severely reduced as the resolution is increased, it is this lack of radiation energy and the accompanying need for long measurement times which has led to the rapid expansion of the Fourier technique as the basic FIR instrument. However the grating does have a number of advantages, namely it is real-time, resolution over a small spectral interval can be improved by closing the splits without a too prohibitively long scan time, it has high contrast, i.e., its spectral purity when used with good blocking filters is very good. This means that transmissions less than 1% can be measured with a high degree of confidence and small, < 0.5%, changes can easily be seen.

articleTitle: >Key Development Items in the Realisation of a 300–500 GHz Heterodyne Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This paper describes the key units such as wideband carcinotron local oscillators, low noise Schottky mixers and lightweight Braggcell spectrum analysers whose development has been undertaken by the European Space Agency (ESA) in order to enable the realization of a high spectral resolution (1 in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>) submillimetre heterodyne spectrometer.

articleTitle: The Effect of Neutron and Gamma Radiation on Liquid Helium Cooled InSb and Ge Bolometers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The ultrasensitive helium cooled bolometers used to measure electron cyclotron emission on tokamak experiments have been found to be sensitive to ionizing radiation as well as infrared radiation. Out tests indicate that for the InSb detector to be used on TFTR in the diagnostic basement area about 20 cm of lead and 60 cm of concrete shielding will be necessary during deuterium-tritium operation.

articleTitle: CH3OH High Resolution Fourier Transform in the Far Infrared
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The FIR absorption spectrum of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH in the 10–85 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> region has been investigated with a resolution of about 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Many Q bands have been resolved and new values for the internal rotation energies could be given.

articleTitle: Wide Band-Pass Filters using Optical Resonance in Metallic Meshes
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Optical resonance in metallic meshes and its use for spectral filtering of far infrared radiation are investigated.

articleTitle: A 0.4K Bolometer Receiver for Millimeter Astronomy
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Engineering tests have been made of a continuum receiver based upon a composite bolometer cooled to 0.4K on the NRAO 36-foot telescope. We will describe some salient features of the receiver design and also discuss the relative sensitivity of this receiver compared to current coherent continuum receivers.

articleTitle: A Coherent 225 GHz Receiver
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A receiver for use at 225 GHz has been designed and built. It uses a low noise, subharmonically pumped, balanced mixer that requires a local oscillator (LO) at only one fourth the signal frequency. The local oscillator is a commercially available 56 GHz phase locked Gunn oscillator with a 50 mW power output. Preliminary results indicate a 12 dB system noise figure (DSB).

articleTitle: A Far Infrared Rooftop Resonator
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Optically pumped far-infrared (FIR) lasers are known to suffer from power instabilities caused by reflected feedback of the pump beam by the FIR resonator [1-3]. To overcome this problem a self-isolating FIR cavity has been constructed using metallic rooftop mirrors as the reflecting elements. See Fig. 1. Cavity isolation is achieved when the incoming pump polarization is oriented at 45° with respect to the crease of the output-coupling rooftop. In this configuration the backward-going pump beam polarization is orthogonal to the input beam polarization. This backward-going feedback beam is then eliminated by a Brewster stack or polarizer. In this way the two cavities are decoupled. Further, since the crease of the input-coupling rooftop is oriented parallel (or perpendicular) to the crease of the output-coupling rooftop, the polarization reorientation described above is repeated. Hence, even if the pump beam makes several passes inside the FIR laser, the polarization of the backward-going pump beam remains orthogonal to that of the forward-going beam. Very significant increases in FIR output power stability have been achieved using this type of self-isolating resonator.

articleTitle: Observations of Electron Cyclotron Emission on the PLT tokamak
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: At the Wurzburg meeting, we reported the installation of an improved radiation collection optical system for the fast-scanning Michelson interferometer that is being used to observe the electron cyclotron emission (ECE) from the PLT tokamak (1). The purpose of this optical system was (a) to provide control over the field of view in the PLT plasma, and (b) to allow the coupling of radiation from a blackbody source to the Michelson to be as much like the plasma-Michelson coupling as possible, in an effort to make absolutely calibrated measurements of the ECE. During the Würzburg meeting, a carbon mirror was installed for us on the far wall of the PLT vacuum vessel so that it served as a viewing target for the optical system. This paper reports on (a) observations of the ECE entering the optical system in two orthogonal directions of polarization that were made following the installation of the viewing target, and (b) the degree of success that has been achieved in an effort to make absolutely calibrated measurements of the ECE spectrum.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Antennae for Electron Cyclotron Emission Measurements on Large Toroidal Plasmas
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In previous electron cyclotron emission (ece) measurement systems, the antennae used to collect the radiation from the plasma and transmit it to the interferometers has in most cases comprised simply of overmoded light pipe close to the tokamak observation window. This crude arrangement has none the less proved adequate in most systems, primarily because the constraints on the directionality of present receiving systems are not very stringent, and because the length of waveguide runs used is relatively short (and consequently not very lossy).

articleTitle: FIR Scattering from Electrostatic Modes at the Ion Cyclotron Range of Frequencies in a Tokamak Plasma
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In order to achieve success in magnetic confinement fusion, ion temperatures in excess of 10keV are required. Ohmic heating of tokamak plasmas is insufficient, and so some form of auxilliary heating is essential. In recent years heating at the ion cyclotron range of frequencies (ICRF) has been under active study as a cost effective and efficient alternative to neutral beam heating [1, 2]. At UCLA experiments aimed at understanding the generation mechanisms and propagation properties of the electrostatic waves produced during ICRF heating have been initiated. These experiments have produced the first direct observation in a tokamak of electrostatic modes in the ICRF.

articleTitle: Wave Guiding of Far Infrared Radiation for the Jet Interferometer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The far infrared interferometer being designed to measure the electron density of the JET plasma will use waveguiding for beam propagation. An experimental 30 m long waveguide set-up is studied, using the 0,195 mm wavelength radiation of a DCN laser. The main characteristics of the guided beam are measured as a function of the angle of incidence. Transmissions up to 60 % are observed and the degree of polarization is kept to a high level in the case of a 60 mm diameter glass waveguide.

articleTitle: Tokamak Temperature Measurement using Electron Cyclotron Emission at the Third Harmonic
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The use of electron cyclotron emission from a tokamak plasma as a means for measuring the electron temperature spatial profile has become popular since the possibility was pointed out by Engelmann and Curatolo [1] in 1973. Generally one uses the fundamental or the second harmonic because the emission from a thermal plasma at these frequencies is very nearly at the black-body level, so that the intensity is directly proportional to the electron temperature and conveniently independent of the electron density. Use of the third harmonic has not been considered attractive because the plasma is optically thin at this frequency so the emission is dependent on the density [2] as well as the wall reflectivity. Unfortunately, as tokamak researchers succeed in creating plasmas of higher densities, the lower harmonic emission can be cut off, so that it does not propagate to the receiving antenna. Under such conditions, the third harmonic becomes more interesting.

articleTitle: Gaussian Optics for Electron Cyclotron Emission Studies of Plasmas
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The formalism of Gaussian Optics is used to analyse optical configurations that are appropriate for plasma diagnostics using the electron cyclotron emission from hot, magnetically confined plasmas.

articleTitle: Injection-Locked Tunable Tea CO2 Laser for SMM Laser Pumping
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: For the ion temperature measurement of Tokamak plasmas by a collective thermal scattering, injection-locked tunable single-mode TEA CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser is being developed as a pumping source for a single-mode submillimeter (SMM) laser. Numerical calculations show that the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser is tunable over 1 GHz and that a pulse shaping is possible. Preliminary experimental tests indicate the feasibility of the scheme.

articleTitle: New Results for Near-Millimeter Wave Isolators and Phase Shifters Based on Magnetoplasmons on GaAs Substrates
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Results are presented for planar “insulated image guide” structures modelling surface magnetoplasmon based non-reciprocal devices for the near-millimeter wave range. Sample results, using GaAs substrates, show acceptable performance for isolators over bandwidths of 65 GHz in the 400 GHz range and of differential phase shifters of bandwidth of 30 GHz in the 550 GHz range for ±5° phase variation.

articleTitle: Computer Analysis of Rectangular Dielectric Waveguide for Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: High dielectric constant rectangular dielectric waveguides are suitable transmission media for millimeter waves. We have made a finite-difference method study of the electromagnetic modes of such guides and determined the limitations of the commonly-used approximate formulas of Marcatili.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optical Ring Resonator Diplexf.rs: Theory and Experiment
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Performance of quasi-optical ring resonator diplexers with plane parallel plate resonator, cylindrical resonator and toroidal resonator mirrors are investigated both theoretically and experimentally. Experimental models have been constructed and tested at 100 GHz. Our results indicate that for diffraction limited cases significant improvement in performance of diplexer may be achieved by utilizing a toroidal reflector properly designed to phase-match the input Gaussian beam from local oscillator.

articleTitle: Rain-Induced Attenuation at 36GHz and 55GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This paper discusses the relationship between the rain-induced attenuation of two vertically polarised line-of-sight mm-wave links at 36GHz and 55GHz. The links share a 4.1km common path across central London and have fading margins of 20dB and 23dB resepctively. Details of the system are given elsewhere {1}. The advantage of a dual frequency measurement is that, since both links share the same propagation path, the attenuation at both frequencies is due to the same volume of rainfall. Thus the rainfall rate is not required and the error introduced by its measurement is eliminated. This technique is also a sensitive indicator of the actual raindrop size.

articleTitle: Continuous Far-Forward Scattering at 10 Microns in a Tokamak
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Small oscillations on the profile of a gaussian beam of radiation emerging from a plasma can be identified with extreme forward collective scattered radiation spontaneously heterodyning with the undeviated beam [1,2,3]. Measurement of these oscillations offers a means of investigating electron density fluctuations at wavelengths so long they scatter within the divergence angle of the probing beam and might hitherto have been dismissed as un-observable.

articleTitle: Flexible Dielectric Waveguide for mm Application using Gore-Tex¯ Expanded Ptfe Dielectric
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A Dielectric waveguide in a cable form fabricated from polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is discussed. The cable construction is a composite of expanded PTFE open cell structure material arranged in such a way that the dielectric constant of cable decreases from the core to the outer surface.

articleTitle: A New Method of Phonon Detection using Time-Resolved Far-Infrared Laser Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A new method of high-frequency phonon detection is reported. By time-resolved far-infrared spectroscopy, transverse acoustic zone-boundary phonons in TlCl and TlBr crystals are observed and the decay of these phonons at temperatures from 3 K to 20 K is investigated.

articleTitle: Reflection and Transmission Spectroscopy of Materials for Near Millimeter Wave Plasma Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We report on Fourier transform reflection and transmission spectroscopy of candidate materials to be used for viewing targets and a blackbody calibration source for near millimeter wave plasma diagnostics. The materials have been chosen for vacuum compatibility and resilience to plasma bombardment and high energy neutron and x-ray fluxes.

articleTitle: Propagation of Visible and Infrared Radiation in Snow and Rain
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: As part of a program to develop improved models for infrared and visible extinction in adverse weather, a one-kilometer transmission range has been established near Houghton, Michigan, where annual rainfall is about twenty inches, fog is common, and annual snowfall often exceeds 200 inches. A Barnes Engineering Transmissometer is used to record transmission in the 3-5 and 8-14 micrometer bands, a Helium-Neon laser transmissometer is used to record transmission at 0.63 micrometers, and a Nd:YAG laser transmissometer is used to measure transmission at 1.06 micrometers. During Transmission measurements, an automated weather station periodically records standard weather parameters. Results are presented as plots of the logarithm of the infrared extinction coefficient versus the logarithm of the visible extinction coefficient (the GAP model format). Extinction coefficients for rain tend to lie along straight lines, in fairly good agreement with the GAP model, when the atmosphere contains rain drops but not suspended droplets. Measured extinction coefficients in snow tend to lie along straight lines on the log-log plots, with slight differences from one snow storm to another, which are attributed to differences in types of snow-flakes.

articleTitle: Laboratory Studies of Water Vapor Absorption in Atmospheric EHF Windows
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A measuring system, comprising a millimeter wave resonance spectrometer and a humidity simulator (RH = 0-101%), for determining absolute absorption by moist air in the 30 to 300 GHz range is described. Performance data and first results obtained at 138 GHz are discussed.

articleTitle: Free Electron Laser Cavity Resonator Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A cavity resonator theory based upon orthogonal mode expansions and scalar diffraction theory is derived. Analytical results are evaluated to describe quantitatively the Columbia free electron laser mirror system. A variety of possible axisymmetric resonator geometries are characterized via an eigenvalue equation.

articleTitle: New CW FIR Laser Emission by Optical Pumping with a Tunable Waveguide CO2 Laser
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A tunable cw waveguide CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser is used to pump far infrared lasers. Further methyl alcohol infrared transitions, inaccessible with conventional sources are detected and investigated using the optoacoustic technique. Stark effect measurements are performed.

articleTitle: Tunable Laser Sideband Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The idea of generating tunable mid-IR signals by mixing stabilized CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser lines with tunable millimeter waves has been put to work in a high-resolution spectroscopic instrument with direct frequency reading. With this instrument, over 100 lines of the R, P, and Q-branches of the n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> fundamental of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F have been measured recently, with ±6.5 MHz absolute accuracy.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Spectral Thermal Emission of the Atmosphere from an Aircraft
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The measurement of the atmospheric thermal emission is important for several reasons. Remote sensing working in the wavelength regions from λ = 3 μm to λ = 5 μm and from λ = 8 μm to λ = 14 μm, with high atmospheric transparency is hampered by absorption and thermal emission of the intervening atmosphere. Furthermore, both the global energy balance and the radiative heating loss of the outdoor surface of building envelopes crucially depend on atmospheric thermal emission |1|.

articleTitle: Calculation of Millimeter Wave Oxygen Absorption Spectra on a Small Microcomputer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Millimeter wave propagation exhibits high absorption behavior near the band centered at 60 GHz and the single line around 118.75 GHz. In this paper, quantum theory will be used to predict line frequencies. A solution for atmospheric attenuation that is amenable to implementation on a very small microcomputer is obtained by using a normalized line shape form.

articleTitle: Magnetic Resonant Three Dimensional Kinetic Theory of the Free Electron Laser with Waveguide Cavity
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Vlasov kinetic theory of F E L employing waveguide laser cavity and helical pump is presented. Distinct from the former theories<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1-5)</sup> this paper has taken into consideration theinfluence of the longitudinal magnetic field and the 3-d structure of the scattered field with the method of plasma kinetic theory. The spatial growth rate formula for the case of magnetic resonance is derived. The results show that the 3-d structure of the field has harmful influence on gain and would even cancel the instability altogether under certain conditions. A condition for eliminating the harmful effect and obtaining the maximum gain is derived and a suggestion employing hollow beams with small wall thickness is made. This theory is a generalization of that by P. Sprangle and R. A. Smith<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(5)</sup> in consideration of the longitudinal field and the 3-d structure of the scattered field.

articleTitle: Theory on Distributed Feedback (DFB) Lasers with Strong Periodic Modulations
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: DFB (Distributed Feedback) lasers do not use conventional resonator mirrors, but provide feedback via backward Bragg scattering from periodic modulations of refractive index and/or gain of the iaser medium. An important feature is the high spectral selectivity which originates in the Bragg effect and allows selection of longitudinal modes |l|. Hitherto, DFB theories were restricted to small modulations |2,3,4,5|. In this paper, we study the effects of strong DFB modulations on the basis of a complex Hill equation which can be solved analytically. This procedure provides for the first time a direct access to the complex characteristics of future DFB lasers with strong modulations.

articleTitle: High Power, 140 GHz Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The design and construction of a pulsed 100 kW, 140 GHz gyrotron will be described. Initial gyrotron operation is expected in late 1981 or early 1982. Advances in gyrotron theory carried out in support of this experimental research will also be described.

articleTitle: General Operational Characteristics of the Gyromonotron
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Extensive research work in recent years has established the gyromonotron as an efficient and reliable source of high power millimeter waves. The gyromonotron has found applications in diverse fields of research, such as plasma heating and metal annealing. Here, we present theoretical studies on the optimal operational characteristics of gyromonotrons as a function of the electron beam energy for both the fundamental and the second cyclotron harmonics. These operational characteristics include interaction efficiency, cavity dimensions, and output power. For both the fundamental and the second cyclotron harmonics, the optimum efficiency remains relatively constant for weakly relativistic electron beams but drops at higher energies. Of particular interest is the fact that second cyclotron harmonic interaction efficiency remains as high as 35% even at a beam energy of only 3 keV. An analytical power scaling relation is presented. Through this relation, the optimal operational characteristics, obtained numerically for a fixed cavity mode, could be generalized to arbitrary cavity modes including, for example, the whispering gallery mode. The generalized operational characteristics cover a wide range of beam energy (3 keV - 1 MeV) and output wave power (a few kW to hundreds of MW). Requirements on the gyromonotron differ greatly from one application to another. Consequently, a general picture of the operational characteristics would facilitate the choice of cavity mode, cyclotron harmonic, beam energy, and cavity dimensions for specialized design analyses.

articleTitle: Subharmonic Mixers for 183–225 GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Subharmonically pumped, balanced mixers have been developed for field measurement systems at 183-225 GHz. These mixers are second and fourth harmonic (X2 and X4) mixers and are designed for use with solid state local oscillators. Preliminary measurements indicate mixer noise figures (DSB) as low as 4.5 dB have been achieved with these devices.

articleTitle: Pump Saturation in Optically Pumped FIR Lasers and Nonlinear Hanle Effect
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The infrared absorption increases in presence of static electric fields explains the enhancements observed in Satrk FIR molecular lasers. Measurements are performed for several transitions of FIR active molecules using a Stark optoacoustic technique. A simple theory is developed for the nonlinear Hanle effect which explains the experimental results.

articleTitle: The Transmission Spectra of Some Potential Radome Materials for Millimetre and Near Millimetre Wavelength Applications
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The power transmission spectra between about 90 and 900 GHz of some woven materials that have been considered for use as the radome in the UK millimetre wavelength telescope facility will be presented. The various electromagnetic and mechanical factors that determine the suitability of such materials for this application will be discussed.

articleTitle: Characterization of GaAs Schottky Detectors in the Submillimeter Range
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We report results in video-detection (.7–3.7 THz) and harmonic mixing (.9 THz) on various Schottky diodes. A comparative analysis is made with respect to parameters such as epilayer thickness or doping, as well as junction geometry.

articleTitle: Nonlinearities of Tungsten-Nickel Point-Contact Diodes: Are we Close to an Understanding of these Puzzling Devices?
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The inherent nonlinearity of high speed tungsten-nickel point-contact diodes employed in harmonic-frequency mixing and frequency measurements in the infrared has been ascribed to electronic tunnelling through the insulating oxide barrier. The requirements necessary for these devices to be used as harmonic generators and mixers in the 2 to 200 THz region are deduced from the available experimental data.

articleTitle: Launching Loss in the Reflection Wideband Gyrotron Travelling Wave Amplifier (Gyro — Twt)
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Experiments<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup> show that the usual 9 db launching loss is absent in the recently proposed wide-band gyro-twt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup>. In the experiment, an input signal is injected from the downstream of the electron beam inside a mildly tapered waveguide. Upon reflection at cutoff, the signal co-propagates with the beam and is amplified. By analyzing the reflection process in detail, we found that the gentle taper of the waveguide produces minimal mode conversion and hence insignificant loss, in agreement with experiments<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1)</sup>. Beam prebunching is also found to be relatively unimportant.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Study of the Grating-Enhanced Excitation of a Far Infrared Surface Wave
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We report a rigorous electromagnetic study of the grating excitation of a far infrared electromagnetic surface wave. We get a surprising result: it exists an optimum groove depth for which the intensity of the surface wave is maximum. The dispersion curve and broadening of the resonance when the groove depth is increased are studied in detail.

articleTitle: Cerenkov Raman Free Electron Lasers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A Cerenkov Raman laser consists of a relativistic electron beam, a dielectric resonator and a rippled magnetic field undulator. In may respects, the device is similar to the usual free electron laser which makes no use of a slow wave structure but it differs in a few important aspects.

articleTitle: Infrared Properties of Quartz Wool
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The ir properties of micro-size amorphous SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> fibres and wool have been investigated theoretically and experimentally at wave-numbers between 400 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and 1400 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Size and shape effects on single scattering have already been discussed at the previous conference |1| in Würzburg. Multiple scattering dominates at higher fibre densities and wool. It differs drastically from single scattering. Therefore, we report here on experiments and theory related to the reflectivity of quartz wool which is ruled by multiple scattering.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in High Power Millimeter Wave Traveling Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Recent work performed at Raytheon on three different types of high power millimeter wave traveling-wave tubes is outlined. The first design addresses the problem of high CW power, while the second focuses on broadband performance. The third is aimed at the non-trival subject of millimeter wave amplifier cost.

articleTitle: Millimeter — Submillimeter Waves and the Rydberg Atoms
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Electronic atomic transitions usually belong to the optical domain. In highly excited states however, they shift towards the far infrared and millimeter wave domain. Let us consider the very simple hydrogen energy spectrum formula: E = − R/n2 where E is the level energy measured from the ionization, R the Rydberg constant and n the principal quantum number. The distance between successive levels DE ∼ n-3 which is in the visible and infrared domain for small n becomes in the millimeter range for n ∼ 30.

articleTitle: Velocity Overshoot in Silicon Inversion Layers by Broad Band Sub-Millimeter Wave Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Small signal velocity overshoot is observed in a Si inversion layer by measuring the dynamical conductivity at d.c. and from 2.5 to 30 cm”<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> (75-900 GHz) in the presence of a heating electric field. An overshoot of 30% is directly observed in the frequency domain. By Fourier transform the hot electron dynamics are displayed on a time scale from .5 to 6.5 psec.

articleTitle: Recent Theoretical Developments in Gyrotron Research
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An electromagnetic radiation mechanism<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-3</sup> known as the “electron cyclotron maser” has been the basis of a new class of radiation devices, called the gyrotrons, capable of generating coherent millimeter and submillimeter radiation at unprecedented power levels. The cyclotron maser interaction takes place between the electromagnetic waves of a cavity or waveguide structure and an electron beam in which the individual electrons move along helical trajectories in the presence of an applied magnetic field. Theory and development of various types of gyrotrons can be found in recent review articles<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4-8</sup> and the references cited therein.

articleTitle: Compact Cyclotron Resonance Maser
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: There is presently considerable interest in the development of rf sources in the millimeter and submillimeter wave frequency region. The proposed application areas include military radar and communications systems, radio astronomy, atmospheric radiometry, nondestructive dielectric testing, detection systems for concealed weapons, fusion plasma heating, and plasma diagnostics. Specific proposed military applications include high resolution radar for target identification, phased array radar configurations, electronic counter-measures and possible covert communications. Reasonable power is necessary because the attenuation at high frequencies is an important factor that limits the range at which objects can be imaged. Airborne applications in addition require that the source be extremely compact (i.e. small size and light weight). These two somewhat contradictory requirements place extreme burdens on the source design. For example, the high voltage or high magnetic fields associated with conventional microwave tubes operating at such high frequencies are not satisfactory. The purpose of the present work is therefore to develop a compact, relatively high power (> 100 W) rf source in the 90-1000 GHz region which does not suffer from these limitations.

articleTitle: A Free-Electron Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A device for the amplification and generation of the unguided TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> gaussian mode of radiation by int eraction of a beam of electrons with the longitudinal electric field of the mode is proposed. Such a device requires that the average electron velocity be greater than the phase velocity of the radiation. Methods for achieving a reduction in the phase velocity of a millimeter wave mode in an open structure are discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Optical Constants of INSB at 4.2K and 1.5K
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The optical constants of indium antimonide at liquid helium temperatures in the spectral region below 40 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> are of particular relevance to the optimal design of detectors for the millimetre and near millimetre wavelength regions. There is, however, little quantitative data of this type in the literature, even though the material has been carefully studied by reflection methods at somewhat shorter wavelengths over its reststrahlen region (1-3). In this work the results of such measurements on InSb by the techniques of Fourier transform spectrometry are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: An Airborne Imaging System at 140 and 220 GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A dual-frequency passive millimeter-wave airborne imaging system has been assembled and flight tested using the Naval Research Laboratory RP-3A aircraft. The system incorporates a 140/220 GHz radiometer built by the Georgia Institute of Technology, and a scanning mirror and a microprocessor controlled data acquisition unit built by the Naval Research Laboratory. The system will be described and selected measurements presented.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Analysis of the Solid State Gyrotron Oscillator
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The solid state gyrotron [1,2] isa promising new source of low power (∼< mW) radiation in the millimeter and submillimeter wavelength region. This region of the spectrum is very difficult to cover with existing technology. IMPATT diodes cooled to 77°K have generated a few milliwatts at frequencies as high as 400 GHz at an efficiency of less than one percent but are extremely difficult to fabricate. Optically pumped “cyclotron maser” have been shown to be not feasible [3]. In fact, no other solid state sources have been demonstrated at submillimeter wavelengths. Lasers are available in this frequency range but are, of course, bulky and expensive. In ref.[2] a linear theory of solid state gyrotron oscillator was developed treating the scattering of electrons phenomenologically. Here we give a nonlinear analysis of the oscillator to calculate the efficiency and the output power of the device. The scattering of electrons is treated more accurately by using the Monte Carlo Method [4].

articleTitle: Submillimeter Heterodyne Astronomy from Mauna Kea
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This paper reports on the results of a collaboration between NASA Goddard Space Flight Center and MIT Lincoln Laboratory in which a laser heterodyne receiver was developed and used at the NASA infrared telescope on Mauna Kea. The NASA IRTF is located on the island of Hawaii at an elevation of 14000 ft (4200 m). The atmosphere from the summit is just barely adequate for submm observations and only days with extremely low water vapor are usable (<1 precipitable mm H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O). This is due to very strong lines of water vapor in the band. Fig. 1 illustrates the atmospheric transmission spectrum at 0.5 mm of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O. At our operating frequency of 691 GHz the atmospheric transmission is about 50%. Observations made during February 1981 showed an atmospheric transmission in this range on three out of the four days on the telescope. However, an earlier observing period in May 1980 produced measurable transmission on two days and the maximum transmission was 20%. The transmission spectrum shown here is an example of what can be expected on a very good day in winter from Mauna Kea.

articleTitle: The Tapered Wall Gyrotron Traveling-Wave Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Gyrotron traveling-wave amplifiers using tapered waveguide circuits are being investigated as a method of obtaining very wide bandwidths at millimeter-wave frequencies. The axial magnetic field is profiled to maintain synchronism. A first experiment using a 70kV, 1 A annular electron beam operating in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> circular-electric mode produced a 13% small signal bandwidth with 18 dB midband gain at 35GHz. A new experiment is being planned which will operated in the TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode with a goal of achieving a two-to-three factor of bandwidth improvement over the first experiment.

articleTitle: Far-IR Observations of Active Regions at Sunspots with a Balloon-Borne 60 cm Telescope
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Far-infrared continuum observations of the sun provide a straightforward method of measuring the temperature of various levels of the transition region between photosphere and chromosphere which is characterized by a temperature minimum. These observations allow the determination of the spectral brightness temperature averaged over the disk as well as structure and variability of the solar atmosphere: center-to-limb variation, solar maps, active regions around sunspots, plages, solar oscillations and flares. Observations of the solar emission spectrum at wavelengths between 10 μm and 1000 μm up to 1975/1976 were reviewed by Mankin |1|.

articleTitle: FIR-Detection in the Presence of High Hydrostatic Pressure
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Hensel et a1. [1] demonstrated that the investigation of the pressure dependence of optical transitions in intraband magneto-spectroscopy is an extremely powerful tool in the analysis of the electronic structure of semiconductors. These authors applied uniaxial stress. Often the application of the complementary hydrostatics tress promises a larger range of information.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Dielectric Constant and Loss Tangent of Thallium Mixed Halide Crystals KRS-5 and KRS-6 at 95GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We report mesurements of the dielectric constant and loss tangent of KRS-5 and KRS-6 at 95GHz. We describe the sample preparation and the waveguide techniques used, and compare our results with values available in the literature (at other frequencies) and a simple theoretical model.

articleTitle: Airborne Millimeter Wave Radiometer for 94/183 GHz High Altitude Atmospheric Measurements
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A moisture sounding imaging radiometer operating at 94/183 GHz has been developed for NASA/GSFC to perform high altitude measurements onboard a WB-57F aircraft [1,2]. The instrument known as the Advanced Microwave Moisture Sounder (AMMS) was used to perform measurements near the 183.3 GHz water vapor line with three data channels and simultaneously collected data at a single window channel at 94 GHz to measure surface emissivity variations over land. The instrument operated under microcomputer control throughout each flight and collected data continuously from aircraft takeoff to landing. The radiometer was integrated into the WB-57F instrumented pallet for a series of data flights between June 1979 and June 1981. A portable ground support system was used following each flight to provide quick-look analysis of the data. The Cooperative Convective Precipitation Experiment (CCOPE) was conducted in the Miles City, Montana area from May through August 1981. CCOPE's main objectives were to study the life cycles of summer convective clouds and storms and to learn how natural processes interact to produce storms. A typical WB-57F data flight during CCOPE involved the aircraft flying above a storm at 18 km altitude within a 150 km radius circle near Miles City. At the same time other aircraft would fly in and around the storm. Other equipment in operation at the same time included ground based weather radar, weather balloons, and a satellite-linked network of 125 ground stations.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetic Resonances of (CH3NH3)2MnCl4 in a Magnetic Field at Arbitrary Angle to the Easy Axis
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We have studied the magnetic excitations of (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> by means of millimeter wave resonance techniques for magnetic fields at various angles to the easy axis. Our results are compared with standard spin wave calculations for the antiferromagnetic resonance and the resonance in the spin flop regime. Surprisingly, we observe a splitting of the resonance lines which increases with increasing angle between the c-axis of the sample and the static magnetic field and which is not described by simple spin wave theory.

articleTitle: On the Submillimeter-Response of a Quasi-Free Carrier Gas in the Presence of a Strong Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The high-magnetic field anomaly in the dielectric response function for submillimeter radiation interacting with a quasi-free carrier system as predicted by Goetze and Hajdu (J.Phys; Cll, 3993 (1978))could not be confirmed experimentally as demonstrated by corresponding experiments in InSb in fields up to 20 Tesla.

articleTitle: Electro-Optic Devices in Dielectric Waveguide
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In recent years, integrated circuit techniques have become increasingly important in implementing components and subsystems at millimeter wavelengths. One common waveguide structure in this spectral region is dielectric image line, formed by placing half-height rectangular dielectric waveguide on a metal ground plane. A number of passive and active devices have been demonstrated using image guide, including directional couplers, filters, phase shifters, scanning antennas, detectors and sources. In most cases, the active devices studied required careful mounting of a discrete electrical device in close proximity to the waveguide structure in a way which optimizes coupling to the waveguide. In this review we describe active devices in dielectric waveguide which can be realized by direct electrical control of the bulk dielectric properties of the transmission medium. These devices have intrinsic high speed, and are directly compatible with common waveguide structures.

articleTitle: A Photopolarimeter for Far Infrared Measurements
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A photopolarimeter has been designed to measure the possible polarization of the Cosmic Background Radiation at millimeter wavelengths. The instrument and the working principle are described together with the testing procedure.

articleTitle: Coupling Losses in Waveguide Lasers Containing a Diffraction Grating
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This paper treats the coupling losses which arise in waveguide CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> lasers when one element of the resonator is a diffraction grating. Line hopping, frequently observed in waveguide lasers, due to the small number of grating facets illuminated, is investi gated.

articleTitle: Far Infrared Spectroscopy of Superconducting NbN
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Transmission data have been obtained between 20 and 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> in NbN films. The results show-strong coupling effects and help in understanding granular behavior.

articleTitle: Measurements of Electron Cyclotron Emission with a Calibrated Fourier Transform Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The calibration of a Fourier transform spectrometer with a liquid nitrogen cooled absorber, measurements of electron cyclotron emission from JIPP T-II, and measurements of transmission loss of radiation guide are described.
