The loss of 0.1∼0.2 dB/m around 5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> has been observed for 50 mm diameter light-pipe.

articleTitle: High Resolution IR-FIR Spectroscopy of Optically Pumped CH3OH Around CO2 9R(10) and 10(34) Laser Lines
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Four new FIR laser lines at 62.88, 48.77, 224.53, and 190.65μm are reported from CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH, optically pumped by the 10R34 and 9R10 lines of a waveguide CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. Measurements performed by several techniques confirm that the pump offsets are ouiside the tuning range of conventional CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> lasers. Two of the lines are assigned as high J transitions within the torsional ground state of the CO stretch.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Raman Laser for Far Infrared Generation
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Semiconductor Raman and Brillouin lasers were proposed to be used for generation of far infrared and submillimeter waves in 1963. We succeded in oscillation of both the LO phonon and TO polariton mode in a GaP crystal. Details on the low threshold lasing condition will be discussed.

articleTitle: A Method to Measure Electron Density in Tokamaks using Electron Cyclotron Emission
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Plasma emission at optically thin harmonics of the electron cyclotron frequency is investigated and a method by which electron density can be determined is discussed. An example from T.F.R. is presented and the potential of this technique for future large tokamaks is explored.

articleTitle: Phase Error Correction in the FTS of Spectra with Positive and Negative Intensities
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The limits of standard techniques of phase error correction in the case of interferograms produced by a source with positive and negative intensities are considered. A solution and some practical examples are presented.

articleTitle: Conventional and Waveguide CO2 Laser as a Pump for FIR Lasers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Far infrared molecular lasers are generally pumped either by a conventional c. w. CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser of by a TEA laser. We have built several waveguide CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> lasers that have been used to excite many new FIR laser lines. A comparison with the conventional laser demonstrates that the waveguide is highly competitive.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Millimeter-Wave Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The state of the art in areas such as material science, solid state devices, and photo-lithography has progressed rapidly and has created a need for innovative and efficient guiding methods of electromagnetic energy. With recent advances in millimeter-wave technology, various transmission lines have been introduced that can be quite useful in the upper frequency bands. By combining classical theory and numerical methods, it is possible to predict the characteristics of these structures and develop a reliable network design that utilizes them. The most common transmission lines may be grouped into four categories: Dielectric waveguides, Semi-open structures, Non-TEM lines, and Quasi-TEM lines. Extensive work has been performed on all of these so reference data is not difficult to obtain.

articleTitle: Intensity Modulation of a Submillimeter Laser with a Schottky Barrier Diode
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We have observed intensity modulation of a submillimeter wave laser at modulation frequency of up to 2GHz. The modulation is achieved by reflecting some of the laser output radiation back into the laser cavity with a Schottky barrier diode.

articleTitle: ECE-Measurements on ASDEX
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The electron cyclotron emission from the ASDEX tokamak has been measured with a novel four-channel polychromator and a conventional Michelson interferometer. A report will be given on the experimental results and the experience gained with these diagnostics.

articleTitle: Self Calibration of Tokamak Electron Temperature Measurements by ECE
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A new method to perform the absolute calibration of the electron temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>) measurement from electron cyclotron emission is presented. Advantage is taken of the difference in the intense plasma emission (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> ≈ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> K) at two cyclotron harmonics. The use of a low intensity reference black-body (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> < 103 K) is eliminated.

articleTitle: Ring Resonators in the Far-Infrared
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The development of a high power (⋍1 MW) narrow bandwidth (≤ 50 MHz), pulsed FIR laser for diagnostic research of fusion plasmas has been an area of great activity over the last few years [1,2]. Until recently [3], all of the schemes investigated have consisted of either stable or unstable linear cavities [4,5].

articleTitle: A Quasi-Optical Scanning Multiport (Quosm) Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Heretofore, guided-wave six-port circuits have been used for network analysis at millimeter wavelengths. A development of an alternative quasi-optical circuit will be described which will provide greater facility at short millimeter to submillimeter wavelengths. It employs an analogue of a Michelon interferometer and near Gaussian-mode propagation.

articleTitle: Some New Aspects of the Electromagnetic Wave Propagation through a Dielectric Medium
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: To the electromagnetic wave propagating through a refractive medium one can assign simultaneously real and imaginary masses. Some consequences of this fact are being explored.

articleTitle: Control of Diffraction Lobes in the Millimeter Region
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A method has been developed to deal with diffraction problems in FIR measurements. The method based on the use of cascaded apertures, will be described. A comparison between theoretical predictions and experimental results will also be presented.

articleTitle: TFTR Fast-Scanning Heterodyne Receiver
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The TFTR fast-scanning heterodyne receiver is designed to sweep the frequency range 75-210 GHz in 3ms in order to measure the blackbody electron cyclotron emission in TFTR, and thus ascertain the time evolution of the electron temperature profile.

articleTitle: Spectrophone Measurements of Water Vapor Absorption Coefficients
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: It is well known that the experimental water vapor absorption coefficients are larger than those generated by theoretical methods [1]. This is readily _, apparent in the region less than 100 cm where calculations using standard line-shapes differ from experimental data by factors of 2, 3 or larger. Explanations for this include incorrect lineshape functions, the presence of dimers or water clusters, or a combined effect due to several causes. Our purpose in doing this experiment has been to generate a large data base including absorption coefficients at several frequencies and for many different combinations of water vapor and total pressure. Hopefully, this data will provide sufficient information in order to generate a more accurate water vapor absorption model and understand the cause of the difference in the experimental and theoretical values.

articleTitle: TFTR 1mm Density Interferometer
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A primary control diagnostic instrument on the Princeton Tokamak Fusion Test Reactor (TFTR) will be a 1mm double-pass interferometer. The interferometer will provide: (a) line average electron density measurements for densities up to 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, (b) a permissive signal for control of neutral beam firing, and (c) an input signal for the gas feedback controlling system that regulates the electron density level. A 1mm wavelength was selected because of the following considerations: 1. A reliable 1 watt carcinotron source is available. 2. The cut-off density for the probing frequency, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, is a factor of 3 above the highest average density to be measured. 3. At 1mm wavelength refraction problems are not severe along the available horizontal mid-plane transmission path (i.e., along the density gradient). 4. Low-loss in over-sized waveguide allows the interferometer to be located remotely from the tokamak and thus minimize environmental problems. 5. The interferometer is relatively insensitive to vibration.

articleTitle: A MM-Wave Collision Warning Device for Helicopters
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A mm-wave radar has been developed having sufficient range to give reliable and timely warning of upcoming obstacles, expecially high voltage transmission lines. A description of the radar as well as first measured results will be presented.

articleTitle: Dielectric Waveguide Circulator
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The design and development of a Y-junction dielectric waveguide circulator which operates in the 35 GHz frequency region is described. The unit consists of a magnesium titanate dielectric waveguide transmission line utilizing Ni Zn ferrite as the gyromagnetic junction material, all of which is mounted on a low permittivity (ε') dielectric substrate.

articleTitle: Far-Infrared Two-Photon Transitions in n-GaAs
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Two-photon transitions in the far-infrared spectral range have been observed for the first time. The photoconductivity of n-GaAs as a function of the applied magnetic field exhibited two-photon transitions between 1s and 2s shallow donor states and two-photon cyclotron resonance. The experimental results indicate that two-photon cyclotron resonance is caused by impurities.

articleTitle: Reflectivity of Some Materials; at 94 GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In order to better understand the characteristics of discrete natural land clutter at millimeter wavelengths, an experimental investigation of the relative reflectivity of various materials at 94 GHz was performed using a substitution technique. The data show that nonconducting materials have a relative reflectivity on the order of 2-3%, and that absorbed water can increase the relative reflectivity significantly.

articleTitle: Measurements of Electron Density and Plasma Current Distributions in Tokamak Plasma
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A submillimeter-wave, phase-modulated polarimeter/interferometer is used for simultaneous time-dependent measurement of line-averaged electron density and poloidal field-induced Faraday rotation along chords of the plasma column in ISX-B tokamak. Heterodyne detection is utilized to achieve the high sensitivity required for the multichord experiment. A data analysis code has been developed to reconstruct the asymmetric distributions of plasma density and toroidal plasma current. The validity of the code and the experimental accuracy have been examined.

articleTitle: The NonLinear Theory of the Free Electron Laser
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The free electron laser (FEL) is a new radiation source characterized by frequency tunability, high power levels, high efficiencies and output wavelengths ranging from the millimeter to beyond the optical regime. The schematic of the FEL configuration consists of a stream of relativistic electrons propagating through a spatially periodic wiggler field as depicted in Fig. 1. Under appropriate conditions, an electromagnetic wave double doppler upshifted in frequency can be amplified.

articleTitle: Heterodyne Spectroscopy with Tunable Laser Sidebands
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Tunable laser sidebands were successfully employed for the first time as a local oscillator in infrared heterodyne spectroscopy. By careful design of a resonant electrooptic modulator, sideband power in excess of 5 mW has been generated from 4W of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser power at a microwave drive power level of 10 W.

articleTitle: Quasiparticle Harmonic Mixing with SIS Junctions
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We have demonstrated quasi particle harmonic mixing of a 36 GHz signal with an 18 GHz local oscillator in tin SIS junctions. Harmonic mixers can have important advantages at high microwave frequencies where insufficient LO power is available.

articleTitle: Some Statistical Properties of Tropical Rainfall Intensity for Centimetre and Millimetre Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The statistical properties of rainfall rate data collected in Ile-Ife are discussed in terms of annual currulative distribution and the frequency of events of peak rainfall rate. Some results of the worst month statistical analysis are reported.

articleTitle: Water Vapor: Its Structure and Electromagnetic Absorption
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Research into the structure of water vapor is reviewed briefly. A physical description is given of the populations and size distributions of neutral molecular clusters in water vapor and moist air that interact with electromagnetic radiation, Some infrared data are given.

articleTitle: A Mm-Wave Raman Free Electron Laser Experiment
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A new experiment has been constructed to study the Raman free-electron laser interaction at millimeter wavelengths. Preliminary measurements, conducted in a superradiant amplifier configuration, indicate the production of tens of MW's of power at approximately 3.5 mm (85 GHz), a wavelength consistent with a coupling of the slow-space-charge wave with the fundamental waveguide mode in the presence of the wiggler field. The radiation conversion efficiency is several percent, an order of magnitude improvement over previous experiments. The parametric dependence of power thresholds and wavelength on pump and guide magnetic fields are found to correlate with a small signal gain analysis of single particle trajectories.

articleTitle: Doppler-Free Optoacoustic Spectroscopy in CH3OH and CH2F2
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The pump offset frequencies of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH and CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> far-infrared(FIR) lasants with respect to the line center of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser have been measured by means of Doppler-free optoacoustic spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Optoacoustic Spectroscopy and FIR Laser Action on CH3Br using a Waveguide CO2 Laser
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The optoacoustic spectrum of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Br around 10 μm band lines of a tunable cw waveguide CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser is investigated. Several new infrared absorptions are observed and most of the corresponding molecular transitions are assigned. Far infrared laser action is reported by pumping with the same CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser: pump offsets are given using the Transferred Lamb Dip (TLD) technique. A new FIR laser emission at 265.8±1 μm is obtained by pumping with the 10-R(20) CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> line and assigned.

articleTitle: Space Charge Effects in a Gyrotron Employing a Solid Electron Beam
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The influence of space charge forces on the performance of a single cavity gyrotron oscillator which uses a solid electron beam was investigated. It was found that space charge effects cause a large efficiency degradation as the beam current is increased, if the other experimental parameters are unchanged. A small increase in the magnetic field, however, can restore the efficiency to higher values.

articleTitle: New Assignments in the Submillimeter Spectrum of Stratospheric Emission
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: New spectroscopic results have been obtained from the data analysis of the stratospheric emission spectrum measured in 1979 from 40 Km altitude in a limb sounding mode with a spectral resolution of 0.0033 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>.

articleTitle: Detector and Mixer Technology for Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: During the past years, a great deal of work has gone into developing low noise mixers and detectors for millimeter and submillimeter waves [1 - 9]. This paper is not intended to provide a comprehensive review of millimeter detector and mixer technology but rather is intended to point out some research areas of current interest. In the following paragraphs, a few comments on the status of Schottky-barrier diodes are made, including recent data [10] on a beam leaded configuration utilized in hybrid integrated circuits. Efforts to increase the burnout capacity of Schottky-barrier diodes and to use of other types of diodes such as TUNNETT and BARITT diodes as high burnout mixers are described. This discussion is followed by consideration of detectors and mixers which operate at cryogenic temperatures - devices based on Josephson and quasi-particle tunneling (SIS) junctions, super-Schottky-barriers and hot electron effects. Some work underway on cryogenic refrigeration is described also.

articleTitle: Optically Pumped Distributed Feedback (DFB) 496 μm CH3F Laser
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Waveguide DFB Theory In previous papers |1| we have reported on the first operation of a DFB gas laser, an optically pumped 496 μm CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F laser with periodic metal waveguide structure |2|. The period of the original waveguide structure was equal to half the laser free-space wavelength, i.e. 248 μm. However, first experiments on the DFB gas laser in operation indicated that the period should be adapted to the laser wavelength modified by the finite cross section of the guide.

articleTitle: Theory of Open Resonators in the form of Waveguide with Slowly Varying Cross Sections
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The general formulas for determining the resonant frequency and diffraction Q value are obtained for an axisymmetric open cavity with any profile. Conical and cylindrical open cavities are analyzed in detail. A comparison with numerical solutions to the conical open cavity problem is made and the agreement is found to be good.

articleTitle: Normal Incidence Millimeter Reflection and Transmission Measurements of Textile Materials
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The magnitudes of the power reflection and transmission coefficients of polyester textile fabrics containing various densities of 8 and 12μm diameter 316 steel fibers were measured at the millimeter frequencies 36.0, 59.0, and 94.0 GHz at normal incidence. Additional data is shown for reflection and transmission extending into the microwave region.

articleTitle: Quasiparticle Tunnel Junctions for MM-Wave Detection
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The paper describes preparation and properties of Pb/In-oxide-Pb(Bi) tunnel junctions for SIS quasiparticle mixer. The effect of repeated thermal cycling on the junction I-V characteristic has been investigated. The present laboratory model of a 70 GHz heterodyne receiver with these devices has a single sideband conversion efficiency just above the classical limit and a mixer noise temperature well below 100 K.

articleTitle: A Microstrip Impatt Diode Oscillator for 100 GHz
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The design and performance of a rugged duroid microstrip impatt diode oscillator is described. The oscillator's frequency was set by a simple, easily replaceable metal resonant cap, with fine tuning of about 30 MHz/mA being achieved by means of the diode current.

articleTitle: An Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigerator for Infrared Bolometers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Adiabatic demagnetization refrigerators have been built and installed in small portable liquid helium cryostats to test the feasibility of this method of cooling infrared bolometric detectors to temperatures below 0.3K. Performance has been achieved which suggests that bolometer temperatures of 0.2K can be maintained for periods of ∼60 hours. Applications to sensitive infrared detection from ground based telescopes and space satellites are discussed.

articleTitle: Microwave Wide Aperture Standard Noise Sources for Antenna Parameters Measurements in Millimeter Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Very accurate antenna parameters measurement technique which implements wide aperture noise sources is described. Construction of the wide aperture microwave noise radiators is discussed. The system can reproduce the noise temperature from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>K to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>K with accuracy 2%-8%.

articleTitle: Optical Tests of Quasi-Optical Components for the MM Region
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The need for various components in millimetersubmillimeter instrumentation has led us to an investigation of several quasi-optical techniques in this wavelength region. Results of studies of laminated TPX lens material, Eccosorb, an efficient quarter wave plate at 225 GHz, and metal grid polarizing beam splitters are presented.

articleTitle: Electronagnetic Coupling between an Infrared Antenna and a 10 μm Laser Radiation using a Corner Reflector
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In an earlier paper /1/ we have studied the. coupling between a long wire antenna and a focused. electromagnetic (EM) beam in order to increase the power coupled to an IR point contact device [MIM or Schottky diode, Josephson jonction).

articleTitle: Comparison of Noise Figure of InP and GaAs Self-Oscillating Mixers
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: GaAs and InP Gunn-effect Oscillators used as self-excited mixers in the 60 GHz frequency range have been investigated. The double side-band noise figure and conversion characteristics was measured and it was shown that the noise performance obtained in these devices makes them attractive for applications where low cost, simplicity in circuitry, and small physical size are important factors.

articleTitle: Photoexcited Cyclotron Resonance in Semiconductors at Far-Infrared
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The far-infrared (84-220 μm) laser cyclotron resonance, impurity-Zeeman absorption and exciton-Zeeman absorption under the intrinsic photoexcitation are described for Ge, Si, InSb and GaAs. Through time-resolved experiments, the optically hot electron state and carrier relaxation as well as recombination mechanism are investigated.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optical Millimeter-Wave Power Combiner
publicationTitle: 1981 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A millimeter-wave combiner using quasioptical open resonators to effectively combine the power output of two InP Gunn oscillators at 60 GHz is described. A combining efficiency of 52% has been achieved in initial measurements.
